subject: Recap: Alpha Initiative — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maya Shah <maya@alphainc.com>; Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@alphainc.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Alpha Initiative — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Hi Maya / Carlos,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning — appreciate you walking us through the Alpha use cases. As promised, a concise recap so we’re aligned on pain, success criteria, and recommended next steps.

1) Key pain points you shared
- Token spend and unpredictable per-request cost on OpenAI for high-volume embeddings and chat flows.
- Vendor lock-in / lack of control over model upgrades and fine-tuning cadence.
- Latency spikes for peak customer-facing flows (billing inquiries, in-app assistant).
- Data residency and auditability requirements for EU customers.

2) Current stack (what you told us)
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (batched via serverless workers).
- Chat assistant: Anthropic Claude for conversational flows; fallback to OpenAI for certain summarization tasks.
- Orchestration: homegrown queue + Redis cache; fronted by GCP (us-central1).
- Auth/data: Tokens stored in GCP KMS; logs forwarded to Splunk.

3) Success criteria for an off-ramp to open models
- <= 1.2x current latency p50 for chat generation under production load.
- Embedding quality >= current embedding producer for retrieval NDCG (internal eval set).
- 30–40% reduction in per-token cost at steady state (target depends on quantization/batching).
- Parity on function-calling / structured outputs and streaming for UX flows.
- Compliance: support for EU region hosting and audit logs compatible with your SOC2 requests.

4) Compatibility & technical constraints
- Need function-calling parity (tooling + structured JSON outputs).
- Streaming responses required for chat — partial tokens delivered to client.
- Max context window for certain long conversations ~100k tokens (summary + KV cache currently used).
- Expectation to reuse current embedding index format (FAISS-based) and not re-embed historical corpus if possible.

5) Initial model shortlist (for POC)
- Llama-2-Chat (70B) — for high-quality chat, test quantized 8-bit paths.
- Mistral-Instruct (13B) — cost-effective instruct tuning for retrieval-augmented flows.
- Falcon-40B-Instruct — good balance for generation-heavy batches.

6) Proposed next steps (owners & timeline)
- Technical workshop / kickoff (90m) with Alpha engs + Redwood infra: week of Mar 30. (Owner: Dev Patel)
- Provide compatibility matrix + runbook (attachment). (Owner: Sean Gallagher)
- POC scope: embeddings parity test (subset), chat latency/quality test, streaming & function-calling demo — 3-week POC. (Owner: Dev Patel)
- Security/Compliance: we’ll send SOC2 + data-handling docs; Alpha to share any additional regs. (Owner: Grace O'Connor)
- Commercial: draft POC quote (credits + engineering hours) & potential Dedicated sizing. (Owner: Vivek Kulkarni)

Attachments: model-compatibility-matrix.xlsx, deployment-checklist.pdf (links below).

If that matches your notes, I’ll schedule the kickoff for Mar 31 and loop in the Alpha engs for a technical deep-dive.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

From: Maya Shah <maya@alphainc.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@alphainc.com>, Alpha Engineering <eng@alphainc.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T17:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Alpha Initiative — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Hi Sean — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Correct on current stack. One nuance: for long context flows we currently materialize summaries every ~20k tokens and store them in Redis. We’d like to avoid a full re-embed if possible (relying on incremental embedding where feasible).
- EU data residency: for EU customers we must ensure embeddings + logs never leave eu-west-1. Can Redwood support regional pinning for the POC?
- Model shortlist looks reasonable — curious about memory/latency tradeoffs for Llama-2-Chat 70B in quantized mode vs Falcon-40B.

Yes to Mar 31 for the technical kickoff. Please include the engs listed and we’ll confirm a time next week. Also please include a rough cost estimate for the 3-week POC (credits + expected infra) ahead of the kickoff so we can clear procurement.

-Maya
Maya Shah
Head of AI Platform — Alpha Inc.
maya@alphainc.com | +1 (212) 555-1290

On Mon, Mar 22, 2026 at 2:05 PM Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Maya Shah <maya@alphainc.com>
Cc: Carlos Ramirez <c.ramirez@alphainc.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T18:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Alpha Initiative — migration off OpenAI/Anthropic to open models

Thanks Maya — all great points. Quick answers and follow-ups: 

- Regional pinning: yes — Redwood Private/Dedicated can pin inference + embedding persistence to eu-west-1 for the POC. Dev will include the steps in the kickoff runbook.
- Incremental embedding: we can validate a 'delta-embed' flow during onboarding so you only re-embed new/changed docs; plan that for the POC.
- Llama-2-Chat 70B vs Falcon-40B: we’ll include benchmark guidance in the compatibility matrix (latency vs quality vs cost). For the initial run we recommend starting with Mistral-13B for embeddings and a 40B-class chat model quantized for latency tests — this gives a lower-cost baseline before attempting 70B.

Action items I’ll own before kickoff (Mar 31):
- POC cost estimate & credits proposal (Vivek to draft commercial).
- Detailed runbook + compatibility matrix (attached).
- Meeting invite for Mar 31 (Dev to set exact time).

If that works I’ll get the calendar invite out by EOD and share the HubSpot POC record + DocuSign if you prefer a simple SOW.

Best,
Sean

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Alpha POC ask & next steps

Quick internal note so we have the ask captured for leadership: 

Summary: Alpha (high-growth SaaS) wants to explore migrating embeddings & chat away from OpenAI/Anthropic. POC scope = 3 weeks: embeddings parity (small subset), chat latency/quality (streaming + function-calls), EU region pinning.

Commercial ask (rec due): propose offering a POC credit package ~ $25k (infra + 2 engineer days) and a follow-on Dedicated sizing discussion. They’re price sensitive — target is net 30–45% reduction vs current spend after optimization.

Risks/needs:
- Engineering support: Dev to lead POC and run benchmarks.
- Security: Grace to send SOC2 + data handling docs; Alpha may request an NDA addendum.
- Exec sponsorship: Vivek — can you OK the POC credit range (25k) or advise lower threshold to approve quickly?

I’ll prepare a one-page POC SOW and HubSpot record today.

Thanks,
Sean
